article.title: Iran's Strategic Leverage in the War
article.summary: Iran has gained leverage in the war by using 'triangular coercion', attacking Gulf states and closing the Strait of Hormuz, which points to a long-term US vulnerability.

article.content_html:
Understanding Triangular Coercion

Iran's strategy of triangular coercion involves attacking Gulf states and closing the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for international oil trade.

Impact on the Region

This move has significant implications for the region, as it affects not only the Gulf states but also the global economy.

US Vulnerability

The US has been criticized for its long-term vulnerability in the region, which Iran has exploited to its advantage.

  • Closure of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted oil trade, affecting global markets.
  • Attacks on Gulf states have raised concerns about regional stability.

Conclusion

Iran's use of triangular coercion has given the country significant leverage in the war, highlighting the need for the US and its allies to reassess their strategy in the region.
